items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: At first, I had a regular field band. Is that right? With Gil Rouge and Perkman.

ctx.x: And how old would you be? How old would you be? About the same age. About the same age. Yeah. About the same age. I don't think. How old were you when you learned how to play the drums?

Oh, I guess. I used to fool at them things when I was just brought up. I think they walked. When the Cotton Exposition came down here, the Sugar and Cotton Exposition, I'm speaking about that, it was way back in 1885. Way back in there. Way back in 1885. My old man happened to buy a drum up there. You know, one of them field drums. There weren't no kettle drums, it was field drums. And he brought it down to me. And then I was about 20 years old, and he made me a present of it. See? And then from then on, I kept…
How old were you when you first started playing for money? For money? Yeah.
